records.title: Effects of physiologically relevant alcohol concentrations on early retinal development: A microfluidic retinal organoid chip analysis.
records.abstract: Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder can lead to aberrant retinal development. However, traditional culture systems fail to avoid alcohol volatilization, leaving the pathogenic mechanisms underlying low-concentration alcohol-induced retinal developmental abnormalities at physiological levels still unclear. In this study, we established a long-term low-concentration (0.03% and 0.1% for 3 weeks) and short-term intoxicating-concentration (0.2% for 24 hours) alcohol exposure model based on microfluidic human retinal organoid chip. We found that long-term 0.1% alcohol exposure leads to reduced proliferation, elevated apoptosis, and severe disruption of the structural organization of the neural retina in human retinal organoids. Using single nuclear RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), we identified a population of abnormal neurons as HuC/D+/Brn-3A- neurons. SnRNA-seq combined with experimental validation revealed a significant increase in this population following alcohol treatment. Furthermore, we identified that impaired energy metabolism in retinal progenitor cells represents the primary mechanism underlying this aberrant differentiation. Alcohol exposure (0.03%) caused a milder phenotype. Additionally, we observed that short-term exposure to intoxication concentrations of alcohol induced developmental delay in human retinal organoids. Notably, Microelectrode Array recordings further demonstrated that alcohol treatment significantly impaired the functional maturation of human retinal organoids. This study identifies impaired energy metabolism as a key driver of alcohol-induced aberrant neurogenesis in human retinal development, providing a mechanistic basis for exploring therapeutic interventions for fetal alcohol spectrum disorder-associated retinal lesions. It also confirms that the microfluidic retinal organoid chip serves as a reliable platform for the toxicological investigation of volatile substances represented by alcohol.

records.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction as a Convergent Mechanism of α-Synuclein Toxicity: A Systematic Review of In Vitro Fibrillar Models.
records.abstract: Synucleinopathies, including Parkinson's disease, Dementia with Lewy bodies, and Multiple System Atrophy, are characterised by intracellular accumulation of misfolded α-synuclein (αSyn). Although αSyn aggregation is central to disease pathogenesis, the mechanisms linking αSyn to progressive neurodegeneration remain incompletely understood. Mitochondrial dysfunction is recognised as a key pathological process, particularly in experimental models using exogenously applied αSyn species, including preformed fibrils (PFFs). This systematic review synthesises evidence from mammalian in vitro studies that examined the effects of disease-associated αSyn conformations, including monomers, oligomers and PFFs, on mitochondrial structure and function. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and PsycInfo were searched to identify eligible peer-reviewed studies published up to March 2026, yielding 33 included studies. Models encompassed neuronal, astrocytic, microglial, endothelial, fibroblast, and induced pluripotent stem cell-derived systems, enabling comparison across cell types, αSyn conformations, and genetic backgrounds. Across included studies, oligomeric and fibrillar αSyn consistently induced mitochondrial depolarisation, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, reduced ATP production, complex-I dysfunction and increased reactive oxygen species generation. Additional mitochondrial pathological changes included fragmentation, cristae disruption, impaired TOM20-mediated protein import, calcium dysregulation, defective mitophagy and increased heteroplasmy i.e. accumulation of damaged mitochondria. These alterations frequently preceded cell death and were amplified in dopaminergic and genetically vulnerable models, including αSyn A53T, SNCA triplication, and PARK2-associated transgenic systems. Our review highlights mitochondrial dysfunction as a mechanism underlying αSyn toxicity, whilst suggesting methodological heterogeneity can limit cross-study translation. Priorities for future research using 'in vitro' models of PFF synucleinopathies include standardised fibril preparation protocols, improved mitochondrial phenotyping, and use of human multicellular and organoid models.

records.title: Forkhead box N1 (FOXN1) in thymus and skin from molecular basis to clinical translation: a review.
records.abstract: Forkhead box protein N1 (FOXN1) is a pivotal transcription factor governing the development of the immune system and cutaneous tissues. This comprehensive review systematically elucidates the molecular structural features of FOXN1, with a particular focus on its essential biological functions within the thymic and cutaneous microenvironments. Specifically, it details the intricate regulation of thymic epithelial cell differentiation, cellular aging, and tissue regeneration, alongside its distinct impacts on skin homeostasis, local metabolism, and accelerated wound repair. Building upon this foundational biology, the article explores the broad clinical phenotype spectrum associated with FOXN1 deficiency, outlining its diagnostic and therapeutic value in conditions such as immunodeficiency, chronic skin disorders, and thymic neoplasms. Furthermore, it highlights cutting-edge translational strategies reshaping regenerative medicine, including FOXN1-based organoid construction and innovative targeted protein delivery systems. Ultimately, this review aims to provide a systematic, multi-disciplinary reference for understanding the pathophysiological significance of FOXN1, effectively bridging basic laboratory insights with advanced clinical applications.

records.title: The role of SARS1 in the progression of colorectal cancer: insights from clinical data and organoid models.
records.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a significant global health concern, with adenomas representing critical precancerous lesions. Early detection of adenomas is essential for reducing the incidence of CRC; however, effective biomarkers for the adenoma-carcinoma transition are currently lacking. Serine tRNA ligase (SARS1) has been identified in colorectal adenoma tissues, but its biological role remains unclear. Here, we analyzed SARS1 expression in colorectal adenoma and colorectal cancer using data from the GEO and TCGA databases, as well as immunohistochemical staining of 48 tissue pairs (normal colorectal mucosa, adenoma lesion, and cancer lesion). SARS1 expression was significantly higher in adenomas and cancers compared to normal colorectal mucosa, decreasing from the adenoma to cancer stages. High SARS1 expression was associated with improved overall survival (OS; Log-rank P = 0.0209) and progression-free survival (PFS; Log-rank P = 0.0147) in patients with CRC. As demonstrated by immunofluorescence and qRT-PCR, in colorectal adenoma organoids, SARS1 knockdown was associated with decreased expression of LGR5 and OLFM4, and increased expression of c-Myc. This gene expression profile mirrors that observed in colorectal cancer organoids, as reported in previous studies. Additionally, the downregulation of SARS1 also enhanced the proliferation of CRC cells and the viability of colorectal adenoma organoids (p < 0.01 to p < 0.0001). Our findings suggest that SARS1 exerts context-dependent, stage-associated growth-suppressive effects during the adenoma-to-carcinoma transition, and its downregulation is associated with colorectal cancer progression. SARS1 represents a candidate marker reflecting adenoma-to-carcinoma progression; however, its clinical utility as a diagnostic or prognostic tool requires independent validation in larger, independent, adequately powered cohorts, and its precise functional mechanisms warrant further investigation.

records.title: Collagen I-rich microenvironments influence cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis in stem cell-derived models of liver development.
records.abstract: Cholangiocyte dysfunction accounts for a substantial proportion of liver transplantations, yet progress towards regenerative therapies is limited by an incomplete understanding of the developmental cues that regulate human cholangiocyte specification and morphogenesis. Here, we established a defined culture system to investigate how collagen I influences hepatobiliary differentiation from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs). Increased collagen I presentation was associated with a bias towards cholangiocyte specification, reduced hepatocyte identity and the formation of branched duct-like tubular structures. Similar effects were observed in primary human foetal hepatoblast organoids, indicating that collagen I-dependent lineage bias is conserved across independent model systems. Mechanistically, collagen I presentation was associated with activation of integrin α2β1- and YAP-associated signalling, while inhibition of collagen-integrin interactions impaired both cholangiocyte specification and tubulogenesis. Together, our findings support a role for collagen I-rich extracellular environments in human hepatobiliary differentiation and provide a defined experimental system for investigating extracellular matrix-dependent mechanisms of bile duct development in vitro.

records.title: MEK2 Suppresses IL-4 Polarization via PPARγ and Negatively Impacts Macrophage Epithelial Crosstalk to Delay Repair.
records.abstract: MEK2 is a highly conserved mitogen-activated protein kinase whose pathway activation is increased in both acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and murine acute lung injury (ALI). We previously demonstrated that leukocyte-specific Mek2-/- mice have accelerated recovery from ALI, including earlier restoration of alveolar barrier function, indicating that leukocyte MEK2 prolongs lung injury. Here, we tested the hypothesis that MEK2 suppresses reparative IL-4-driven macrophage function. Transcriptional profiling of WT and Mek2-/- bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) revealed that MEK2 inhibits a subset of IL-4-dependent gene expression, including those enriched in wound repair pathways. Mechanistically, MEK2 is required for IL-4-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation and the suppression of PPARγ levels. Pharmacologic inhibition of PPARγ abolished the enhanced IL-4-dependent gene expression observed in Mek2-/- BMDMs, identifying PPARγ as a key mediator by which MEK2 restrains reparative macrophage polarization. To determine the functional relevance of these findings, we evaluated macrophage-supported alveolar epithelial type II (AT2) cell growth using an alveolar organoid model. IL-4-polarized macrophages enhanced AT2 proliferation in a PPARγ-dependent manner, whereas MEK2 suppressed this reparative effect. Together, these findings identify MEK2 as a negative regulator of reparative macrophage programming via suppression of PPARγ. Targeting MEK2 may represent a novel therapeutic strategy to accelerate repair of lung injury via enhancement of PPARγ activity in reparative macrophages.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Structural mechanism of programmable gene integration by the R2 retrotransposon coupled with CRISPR-Cas9.
records.abstract: R2 retroelements are non-long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons that primarily insert into 28S ribosomal DNA loci across diverse eukaryotes. R2 elements home to their target sites through target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT), in which the R2 protein recognizes and nicks the target DNA to prime reverse transcription using an R2-encoding RNA as the template. The avian R2 system from Taeniopygia guttata (R2Tg) can insert a payload sequence within an RNA template into 28S ribosomal DNA loci in human cells. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy structures of the R2Tg-template RNA-target DNA complex in the TPRT initiation state, both alone and bound to a Cas9-guide RNA complex. These structures provide mechanistic insights into R2Tg-mediated TPRT in its natural context and in the programmable gene integration system STITCHR (site-specific target-primed insertion through targeted CRISPR homing of retroelements). Furthermore, we combine these structural insights with computational protein design methods to engineer an enhanced STITCHR system.

records.title: Application of computational methods in the drug discovery and development of Alzheimer's disease.
records.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder marked by the accumulation of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles in the brain, leading to cognitive decline. As the most common dementia, AD affects over 50 million individuals worldwide, with 10 million new cases each year. Despite many significant progresses in AD research fields, there is still no effective treatment. Advances in molecular modelling and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm have facilitated the application of computational methods in AD drug development, offering advantages in terms of efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and resource conservation. These strategies, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, protein structure prediction, virtual screening, and de novo drug design, have been widely employed in the past decades. Additionally, AI pharmaceutical companies have revolutionized the traditional drug development pipeline such as AD biomarker discovery, accurate diagnosis and precision medicine, etc. This review offers a thorough summary of recent progresses in computational-based methodologies in the study of AD drug development, including the elucidation the pathological mechanism at the molecular level, target identification, target 3D structure prediction, lead compound discovery, de novo molecular generation, multi-target directed ligands, drug repurposing, biomarker discovery, etc., showing promising applications of molecular modelling and AI in the development of AD therapy.

records.title: Structure-Function Relationships of Cid1 Poly(U) Polymerase: Catalysis, Substrate Recognition, Engineering, and Applications.
records.abstract: RNA 3'-end modification is an important regulatory mechanism that influences RNA processing, stability, localization, function, and degradation. Beyond its biological roles, RNA 3'-end modification has become a valuable tool in biotechnology, enabling applications in RNA labelling, sequencing, engineering and oligonucleotide synthesis. Terminal nucleotidyltransferases are key enzymes responsible for template-independent nucleotide addition to RNA molecules. Among these enzymes, Schizosaccharomyces pombe Cid1, a poly(U) polymerase, has emerged as an important model for understanding RNA-specific terminal nucleotidyltransferase activity. Structural and biochemical studies have revealed how nucleotide recognition, metal-ion-dependent catalysis, RNA positioning, and conformational dynamics regulate Cid1-mediated uridylation. Recent advances in protein engineering, molecular simulation, machine learning, and generative protein design have further expanded Cid1 functionality, generating variants with improved activity, altered substrate specificity, and potential applications in enzymatic RNA synthesis. This review summarizes the biological functions, structural characteristics, catalytic mechanisms, protein engineering strategies, and emerging biotechnological applications of Cid1, as well as the remaining challenges, highlighting its potential as a programmable platform for RNA 3'-end functionalization and enzymatic RNA oligonucleotide synthesis.

records.title: DRAGON-3D: an electron-density-aware generative model for dual-target drug molecule generation.
records.abstract: Dual-target drug molecule generation is a significant computational challenge due to the structural constraints imposed by two protein binding pockets. Existing generative models typically rely on scarce dual-target drug datasets and struggle to capture three-dimensional (3D) structural and physicochemical interactions between protein pockets and ligands, limiting generalization to new target pairs. To address these limitations, we propose DRAGON-3D, a general dual-target drug molecule generation model based on latent-space fusion of 3D electron-density representations of diverse target pairs. Our model employs a novel bi-Net β-VAE architecture and an innovative dual-pretraining strategy, enabling dual-target molecule generation using only single-target data. By integrating 3D spatial electron-density with 2D molecular topology, DRAGON-3D enhances generalization and spatial compatibility across diverse dual-target protein pairs. Comprehensive benchmarks show that DRAGON-3D is a promising framework for the generation of candidate dual-target molecules, particularly in molecular diversity, drug-likeness (QED), deployability, generalizability, and interpretability. Overall, DRAGON-3D provides an efficient, interpretable, and electron-density-informed paradigm for de novo dual-target molecular generation.

records.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design.
records.abstract: Small protein scaffolds enable precise targeting but often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity and immunogenic liabilities. Here we develop Chimeraffibodies (CABs), a linker-free bispecific scaffold class that encodes interdomain geometry through seamless α-helix sharing. CABs are designed by AlphaSync, a structure-design framework that defines domain orientation through closed-form exhaustive local rigid-body superposition and ProteinMPNN-based sequence refinement. Using HER2-binding affibody and an albumin-binding domain, we generated 861CM, which preserved parental paratopes while enforcing a defined shared-helix architecture. Structural, biophysical and cellular analyses demonstrated stable assembly, cooperative target recruitment and retained affinity, with HSA binding of ∼14.3 pM and HER2 binding of 610 pM in the albumin-bound state. In vivo imaging revealed sustained tumor localization, reduced hepatic and renal background and improved organ-to-tumor contrast. CABs establish helix sharing as a geometry-encoded strategy for generating compact, homogeneous, and pharmacokinetically optimized bispecific proteins.

records.title: EquiDesign: a versatile computational framework for de novo protein sequence design.
records.abstract: Designing amino acid sequences that uniquely fold into target three-dimensional conformations defines the protein inverse folding problem, a formidable bottleneck in de novo protein design. Current computational paradigms, including deep learning-based approaches, often struggle to reconcile high sequence accuracy with structural stability, computational efficiency, and generalizability across diverse protein families. Here, we present EquiDesign, a deep learning framework that surmounts these constraints via a novel multistep Equiformer-enhanced architecture. By disentangling geometric features into invariant scalars and equivariant vectors, EquiDesign preserves the intrinsic directional topology of the protein backbone during message passing. This is achieved through spatial K-nearest neighbor graph construction and geometric attention mechanisms that hierarchically fuse multiscale contextual information, yielding a physically grounded representation of protein conformations. Extensive benchmarking demonstrates that EquiDesign achieves superior sequence recovery on standard and challenging test sets compared with state-of-the-art methods. Critically, the generated sequences exhibit exceptional structural fidelity, folding stability, and sequence diversity, as validated by comprehensive controls against training-set memorization, compositional bias, and physical energy landscapes, alongside targeted diversity sampling. These results establish EquiDesign as a robust, scalable, and generalizable inverse folding solution, driven by SE(3)-equivariant encoding and multiscale geometric attention, thus propelling de novo protein design toward unprecedented structural precision.

records.title: FGFR Alterations in Bladder Cancer-From Molecular Pathogenesis to Precision Oncology.
records.abstract: Alterations in the fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) pathway, particularly FGFR3, are among the most common genomic events in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and represent a cornerstone of precision oncology. Although FGFR3 alterations predominate, selected FGFR2 fusions also identify patients who may benefit from targeted therapy. This review summarizes the biology, molecular diagnostics, and evolving clinical applications of FGFR alterations in UC. FGFR2/3 alterations are clinically actionable biomarkers across non-muscle-invasive, muscle-invasive, metastatic, and upper-tract UC. Comprehensive genomic profiling, tissue sequencing, plasma circulating tumor DNA, urine-based molecular assays, and molecular residual disease assessment are expanding their roles in diagnosis, treatment selection, surveillance, and disease monitoring. Recent clinical studies support combination strategies, next-generation FGFR inhibitors, and earlier use of FGFR-directed therapy, while emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence-assisted pathology and integrated multi-omic biomarkers, may further improve patient selection. FGFR alterations have become integral to the molecular classification and precision management of UC. Continued advances in molecular diagnostics, liquid biopsy, biomarker-guided therapy, and next-generation FGFR inhibitors are expected to further personalize care. This review provides a practical framework for integrating FGFR biomarkers into contemporary management and highlights emerging developments likely to influence future clinical practice.

records.title: Immune cell-derived exosomes in the tumor microenvironment: mechanisms of immune evasion and emerging therapeutic strategies in cancer immunotherapy.
records.abstract: Tumor-released exosomes have emerged from the shadows of "cellular dust" to be recognized as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment (TME). These nano-sized vesicles (30-150 nm) carry a complex cargo of proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids that profoundly reshape anti-tumor immunity. This review comprehensively examines the dualistic nature of immune cell-derived exosomes in cancer progression, with particular focus on exosomes originating from B lymphoma cells, T lymphocytes, natural killer (NK) cells, and myeloid-derived suppressor cell lineages including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), mast cells, and neutrophils. We delineate the mechanistic pathways through which these exosomes disrupt the cancer immunity cycle suppressing CD8+ T cell activation via PD-L1/PD-1 engagement, inducing lymphocyte apoptosis through FasL and TRAIL, promoting regulatory T cell expansion, polarizing macrophages toward the M2 immunosuppressive phenotype, and establishing pre-metastatic niches through MMP-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling. The molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis including ESCRT-dependent and ceramide-mediated pathways is critically reviewed, alongside the selective packaging mechanisms that concentrate immunosuppressive miRNAs (miR-155, miR-21, miR-23a, miR-223) into exosomal compartments. Importantly, we highlight the emerging therapeutic premises targeting these vesicles: pharmacological inhibition of exosome secretion (GW4869, Rab27a knockdown), checkpoint blockade reversing exosomal PD-L1-mediated T cell exhaustion, and the engineering of immunostimulatory exosomes as cell-free cancer vaccines establishing exosomes not merely as biomarkers of disease progression but as actionable therapeutic targets. The clinical translation of exosome-based diagnostics including liquid biopsy platforms detecting circulating tumor-derived exosomes and therapeutics that include engineered exosomes delivering immunomodulatory cargo represents a frontier in precision cancer immunotherapy.

records.title: Cellular origins and evolutionary dynamics of plasma cfDNA in solid tumors: integrating germline, tumor-derived, and hematopoietic variation for MRD and treatment guidance.
records.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a heterogeneous and rapidly changing biological pool derived from malignant cells, normal tissues, and hematopoietic cells. The abundance and molecular composition of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) are determined not only by tumor burden but also by tissue architecture, vascular access, cell-death programs, chromatin organization, nuclease processing, systemic clearance, treatment exposure, and clonal evolution. These biological determinants shape the mutation, methylation, fragmentation, nucleosomal, and temporal features exploited by contemporary liquid-biopsy assays. Accurate clinical interpretation therefore requires both sensitive detection and reliable source attribution, particularly the distinction of tumor-derived variants from constitutional germline alterations and clonal hematopoiesis. In this review, we integrate the biological origins and processing of plasma cfDNA with analytical strategies for low-tumor-fraction detection and critically evaluate the evidence supporting postoperative molecular residual disease (MRD), recurrence surveillance, treatment-response assessment, resistance monitoring, and ctDNA-guided therapy across solid tumors. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing prognostic validity, treatment-predictive value, and demonstrated clinical utility. Current evidence is strongest in colorectal cancer and, more recently, ctDNA-selected urothelial cancer, whereas routine ctDNA-directed intervention in resected non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer remains insufficiently validated. By linking cfDNA biology to an explicit hierarchy of clinical evidence, this review defines both the established applications and the major limitations that must be addressed before broader implementation of ctDNA-guided precision oncology.

records.title: Clinical utility of circulating tumor cell PD-L1 expression for predicting immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in esophageal cancer.
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in esophageal cancer, yet reliable biomarkers remain lacking. Tissue PD-L1 testing is limited by intratumoral heterogeneity and invasiveness, whereas circulating tumor cells (CTCs) offer a non-invasive alternative. This study evaluated CTC PD-L1 expression as a predictive and prognostic biomarker in patients with advanced esophageal cancer receiving chemo-immunotherapy. A total of 93 patients with stage III-IV esophageal cancer were enrolled. The primary biomarker analysis was restricted to 59 patients who received chemo-immunotherapy, while 34 patients treated with chemotherapy alone were analyzed separately. Baseline CTCs were isolated and PD-L1 expression assessed, alongside tissue PD-L1 (tPD-L1) by immunohistochemistry. Associations with objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using ROC curves and univariate and multivariable Cox regression. CTC positivity correlated significantly with advanced stage, metastasis (p = 0.0411), and larger tumor size (p = 0.0454). In the chemo-immunotherapy cohort, CTC PD-L1 positivity was associated with a higher ORR (75.0% vs. 29.6%, p < 0.001) and showed moderate predictive ability (AUC = 0.7049, p = 0.0037). CTC PD-L1 positivity was significantly associated with OS (HR = 0.254, p = 0.002), but not significantly with PFS in univariate analysis (HR = 0.546, p = 0.042; Kaplan-Meier p = 0.061). Conversely, tPD-L1 status was not significantly associated with PFS or OS (both p > 0.05). In multivariable analysis adjusting for age, sex, histological subtype, stage, metastasis, and treatment modality, CTC PD-L1 remained an independent prognostic factor for PFS (HR = 0.488, p = 0.039) and OS (HR = 0.244, p = 0.002). Baseline CTC PD-L1 expression was associated with favorable response and OS in patients receiving chemo-immunotherapy, and may complement tissue testing. These exploratory findings require prospective validation in larger cohorts before clinical use.

records.title: Non-invasive prediction of olfactory recovery in severe CRSwNP: a cross-compartment translational nomogram based on secretory IL-17A.
records.abstract: Predicting olfactory recovery after surgery for severe chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) remains challenging. To overcome the reliance on invasive tissue biopsies, this study aimed to identify non-invasive liquid biopsy biomarkers reflecting the deep mucosal inflammatory microenvironment, ultimately developing a point-of-care prognostic model. A "tissue-to-secretion" dual-cohort validation strategy was employed. A Random Forest (RF) algorithm screened deep-tissue proteomes (Luminex) in a discovery cohort (N = 67). An independent RF model evaluated non-invasive nasal secretions (Olink) in a validation cohort (N = 62). Bidirectionally convergent targets were assessed for continuous dose-response relationships with absolute olfactory improvement [Δ(visual analog scale)VAS] score at 6 months. A clinical-molecular nomogram was developed and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The tissue-based RF identified interleukin (IL)-17A as a core prognostic candidate. The independent secretion-based RF model also prioritized secretory IL-17A, achieving bidirectional convergence. While canonical Type 2 cytokines (IL-5, IL-13) lost predictive significance in secretions (P > 0.05), secretory IL-17A demonstrated a robust dose-response correlation (r = 0.334, P = 0.0003) and emerged as an independent protective factor for olfactory recovery ([odds ratio] OR = 1.408, 95% [confidence interval] CI: 1.03-2.03). The joint nomogram, seamlessly integrating baseline VAS and secretory IL-17A, yielded an optimism-corrected (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) AUC of 0.793 (95% CI: [0.6908-0.9079]) with adequate calibration and substantial net clinical benefit. Through cross-compartment translation, we identified secretory IL-17A as a robust, non-invasive indicator of mucosal plasticity and olfactory reversibility. The derived joint nomogram provides an actionable framework for personalized pre-operative counseling and risk stratification in severe CRSwNP.

records.title: The evolving landscape of DLL3-directed Therapeutics in small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) remains one of the most lethal thoracic malignancies, characterized by rapid progression, early metastasis, and limited durable responses to conventional therapy. Delta-like ligand 3 (DLL3), a Notch pathway inhibitory ligand aberrantly overexpressed on the surface of approximately 70-85% of SCLC tumor cells but largely absent from normal adult tissue, has emerged as a compelling and therapeutically actionable target. Early efforts to exploit DLL3 through the antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) rovalpituzumab tesirine (Rova-T) yielded important mechanistic insights despite failing to demonstrate survival benefit in phase III trials and have since catalyzed a new generation of more refined DLL3-directed strategies. This review critically examines the evolving portfolio of DLL3-targeted therapies across three principal modalities: T-cell engagers, ADCs, and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies. In parallel, we examine emerging non-DLL3 therapeutic strategies reshaping the broader SCLC landscape. We additionally discuss the translational science underpinning DLL3 as a biomarker, including the emerging roles of circulating tumor cell-based liquid biopsy and DLL3-directed immunoPET-CT imaging in patient selection and treatment monitoring.
